brief: Explain eigenvectors in 90 seconds, narrated, 16:9 and 9:16.
requirements: Duration: 90 seconds (verifier tolerance 2 s) in every delivered format
Two video deliverables: 16:9 and 9:16, each exact geometry - both formats shipped, not one standing in for the other
Narrated: continuous spoken narration with a real audio stream in the mix
Language: narration and on-screen text in English (the request's language)

Content: explains eigenvectors themselves - the intuition (a vector the transformation only scales, never rotates) and the relation Av = lambda*v (eigenvalue times eigenvector), with at least one worked example
Claims: every on-screen mathematical claim is verified (sympy proof / claims ledger) - no unverified math
The 9:16 deliverable is composed for vertical (format-aware re-layout, safe area holds) - not a letterboxed or center-cropped 16:9
One audio mix at the studio loudness target (narration intelligible: LUFS within 1, true peak <= -1 dBTP)
Scope: the segment durations sum to the 90 s target (no over-scoping into a longer treatment)
must_not: must not deliver only one format or fake the second (a center-crop or letterbox of the 16:9 is not a 9:16 composition)
must not treat the 90 seconds loosely (a 60 s or 2-minute piece fails the ask; the segments must not over-scope the target)
must not pick a technique that cannot narrate (plain motion has no narration voice of its own - narration is an explicit ask)
must not put unverified math on screen (every claim needs a sympy proof / claims-ledger entry)
must not invent inputs (no source footage or files are needed; none may be flagged or fabricated)
must not switch language (the request is English; narration and on-screen text stay English)
